title: Accorder selon la fonction, pas la proximité
summary: Find preceding direct objects, distinguish reflexive roles and handle infinitives and invariable participles.
objectives: Apply avoir agreement with object pronouns and relative que.
Avoid agreement with indirect objects and common invariable constructions.
Distinguish the subject and object of a following infinitive.

sources.label: Public lesson consulted to identify benchmark scope for preceding-object agreement

sections.title: Ask what the participle's direct object is
paragraphs: A direct object (COD in French grammar) attaches without à or de; an indirect object (COI) depends on a preposition in the underlying construction. With avoir, a participle agrees with its direct object only when that object comes before it. Neither the closest noun nor the subject automatically controls agreement.

A preceding le/la/l'/les or relative que can represent the direct object. Find its referent, then choose masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine/mixed plural or feminine plural: pris, prise, pris, prises; fait, faite, faits, faites; écrit, écrite, écrits, écrites. Most regular forms add -e, -s, -es: envoyé, envoyée, envoyés, envoyées.
Lui and leur are indirect here and do not trigger agreement. Dont represents a de relationship and is not a direct object. A following direct object also leaves the participle unchanged.

examples.note: The direct object follows the participle.
Les represents a feminine plural preceding object.

examples.french: La décision que nous avons **prise** est définitive.
examples.english: The decision we made is final.
examples.note: Que represents la décision, feminine singular.
Écrire à someone: leur is indirect.

examples.french: Les projets dont nous avons **parlé** avancent.
examples.english: The projects we discussed are progressing.
examples.note: Parler de: dont is not a direct object.

mistakes.avoid: Les lettres que j'ai écrit sont courtes.
mistakes.prefer: Les lettres que j'ai écrites sont courtes.
mistakes.why: Que is the preceding feminine plural direct object of écrire.

sections.title: Être does not make every reflexive participle agree with the subject
paragraphs: A reflexive pronoun refers back to the subject, but its function still matters. In elles se sont lavées, se is what they washed: it is a preceding direct object. In elles se sont lavé les mains, les mains is the following direct object; se means 'to/for themselves' and is indirect.

Se parler and se téléphoner have indirect se because one parle/téléphone à quelqu'un. A preceding direct object other than se can still control agreement: les mains qu'elles se sont lavées. Essentially pronominal verbs such as s'enfuir normally agree with their subject; do not force the direct/indirect paraphrase onto every lexical pronominal verb.

examples.note: Se is direct; the dancers are women.
Un repas is the following direct object.

examples.english: The two neighbours phoned each other.

mistakes.why: Parler à gives an indirect se; there is no direct object triggering agreement.

sections.title: Infinitives and special non-object readings
paragraphs: Before an infinitive, vu and entendu agree with a preceding direct object when that referent performs the infinitive's action: les musiciennes que j'ai entendues jouer. In les œuvres que j'ai entendu jouer, the works do not perform the playing; que is the object of jouer, so entendu stays unchanged.

Fait immediately followed by an infinitive is always invariable, even when a feminine or plural object precedes it: les portes que j'ai fait réparer. For laissé + infinitive, the 1990 spelling recommendations permit invariable laissé throughout; traditional agreement follows the performer distinction. Both conventions should be respected consistently.

When en is the direct-object pronoun meaning 'some/of them', the participle normally stays unchanged: des erreurs, j'en ai commis. This does not cancel agreement with a separate preceding direct object: les conclusions que j'en ai tirées. Neutral le/l' representing a whole idea is invariable. Amounts after coûter, peser or durer are often measures, not direct objects: les cent euros que cela a coûté; a genuinely transitive figurative use can agree: les efforts que cela a coûtés.

examples.french: Les choristes que j'ai **entendues** chanter étaient excellentes.
examples.english: The female choristers I heard singing were excellent.

examples.french: Les chansons que j'ai **entendu** chanter étaient anciennes.
examples.english: The songs I heard being sung were old.
examples.note: The songs do not perform the singing.

examples.french: Ces fenêtres, je les ai **fait** remplacer.

examples.note: En is the object; the usual form is invariable.

examples.french: Elle est plus patiente que je ne l'avais **cru**.
examples.english: She is more patient than I had thought.
examples.note: L' stands for an idea, not a feminine person.

examples.french: Les deux heures que le trajet a **duré** ont été pénibles.
examples.english: The two hours the journey lasted were difficult.
examples.note: The duration is a measure, not a direct object.

practice.prompt: Supply only the participle of choisir: Ces affiches, je les ai ___ moi-même.
practice.explanation: Les represents feminine plural affiches before the verb.

practice.prompt: Supply only the participle of prendre: Voici les photos que tu as ___.
practice.explanation: Que is the preceding feminine plural direct object.

practice.prompt: Supply only the participle of laver: Elle s'est ___ les cheveux.
practice.explanation: Les cheveux follows the verb; se is indirect.

practice.prompt: Supply only faire's participle: Les chaises que nous avons ___ réparer sont solides.
Supply only écrire's participle: Les réponses qu'il a ___ sont précises.
Supply only répondre's participle: Les clientes ? Nous leur avons ___.
Supply only rencontrer's participle: Ces deux femmes se sont ___ au marché.
Supply only téléphoner's participle: Elles se sont ___ dimanche.
Supply only voir's participle: Les athlètes féminines que j'ai ___ courir sont arrivées.
practice.explanation: The preceding referents perform the running.

practice.prompt: Supply only voir's participle: Les maisons que j'ai ___ construire sont habitées.
practice.explanation: The houses are built; they do not perform construire.

practice.prompt: Use the usual invariable form with direct-object en. Supply only lire's participle: Des revues, j'en ai ___ plusieurs.
practice.explanation: En normally leaves the participle unchanged.

practice.prompt: Supply only coûter's participle for a monetary measure: Les cinquante euros que cela a ___ étaient prévus.
practice.explanation: The amount is a measure, not a direct object.

practice.prompt: Supply only faire's participle: Cette tarte, c'est moi qui l'ai ___. No following infinitive.
practice.explanation: Ordinary faire agrees with preceding feminine l'; the infinitive exception does not apply.

practice.prompt: Supply only tirer's participle: Les leçons que j'en ai ___ sont utiles.
practice.explanation: Que is the direct object; en has a separate 'from it' role.

practice.prompt: Use the 1990 invariable convention. Supply only laisser's participle: Les voyageuses que j'ai ___ passer m'ont remercié.
practice.explanation: This prompt specifies the invariable convention; traditional laissées is also legitimate under the traditional rule.

practice.prompt: Supply only enfuir's participle: Les prisonnières se sont ___.
practice.explanation: S'enfuir is essentially pronominal and agrees with its subject.

production_task.prompt: Write a short report on a repaired community hall. Mention objects you selected, something you had repaired, and two volunteers' reciprocal communication. Use preceding objects deliberately.
production_task.model_answer: Les lampes que nous avons choisies éclairent bien la salle. Les prises que nous avons fait remplacer sont maintenant sûres. Les deux bénévoles se sont téléphoné pour organiser la suite.
production_task.translation: The lamps we chose light the room well. The sockets we had replaced are now safe. The two volunteers phoned each other to organize the next steps.
rubric: Identify each participle's direct object before checking agreement.
Fait before an infinitive stays invariable.
Indirect reciprocal se does not trigger agreement.
The report distinguishes your decisions from work performed by others.
